q1: How are the two range-level seeding assignments related within one retained EU?

Evidence: "Within an EU, seeding is randomly assigned to one range and not the other. The authors explicitly say the Medicine Bow assignment plot would have the opposite shading from the Sierra Madre plot."

This directly states that within an EU, one range gets seeding and the other doesn't. The "opposite shading" confirms complementary assignment. One joint allocation selects the seeded range, and the other range receives the complementary unseeded assignment.

So q1 = complementary_assignment.

q2: Does an assigned-unseeded label, by itself, establish zero physical exposure to seeding material in this study?

Evidence: "Slide 24 reports ground-based ice-nucleus measurements indicating that silver iodide reached Medicine Bow in 21 Sierra Madre seeding cases. Slide 29 reports 18 modeled cases of enhanced precipitation in Medicine Bow during Sierra Madre seeding..." 

This shows cross-range contamination - silver iodide reached the unseeded range (Medicine Bow) when Sierra Madre was seeded. So the assigned-unseeded label does NOT establish zero physical exposure. It establishes the planned allocation, while physical exposure requires additional evidence because cross-range contamination is discussed.

Scope says: "auxiliary gauges and possible cross-range contamination do not redefine the assigned treatment." This means assignment is the treatment label, but physical exposure is separate.

So q2 = assignment_only.
